author: agent:claude-code
message: The chained-bulge attempt at the Schur todo, measured and reverted, and what the todo now needs.

title: Chained bulges made no difference at 300-400
body: Hypothesis: at 300 x 300 and up, h and the Schur vectors outgrow the 1 MB L2, so each one-bulge sweep streams them from L3, and chasing the round's shifts as one chain (bulges three rows apart, the lowest first at each step, which reproduces the sequential sweeps exactly) would cut that traffic by the number of bulges. Measured best-of-3 in one build: 200 9.0 vs 9.2 ms, 250 17.0 vs 16.9, 300 25.1 vs 25.6, 400 56.8 vs 55.7 (per-pair sweeps vs chain): no difference, so the sweeps aren't bound by memory traffic and the chain was reverted. Lesson: the update kernels run at about a third of the core's arithmetic peak with their data in cache; LAPACK's edge at 400 comes from its blocked updates (each window's reflectors accumulated and applied as FMA matrix products), which on this CPU would at best draw level. At 400 the time is about 37 ms in sweeps and 12 ms in AED rounds.

schur is about 0.9x scipy.linalg at 300 / 400 (Lyapunov is ahead there). A chain of bulges with direct updates was measured and gave nothing (see the misstep 'Chained bulges made no difference at 300-400'). What's left is dlaqr5's blocked scheme: accumulate each window's reflectors into an orthogonal U and update off-window rows, columns and the Schur vectors with FMA matrix products (exploiting U's block structure), plus a cheaper AED (12 ms of 49 at 400). Expected payoff on Zen 4: about parity; worth it only if sizes above 300 matter.
